title: SDK migration: unify retry/backoff behavior & streaming ergonomics for v2 (Py/TS/Go)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are executing the SDK v1->v2 migration work focused on three interlocking areas: (1) standardized retry semantics and default backoff across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, (2) improved streaming ergonomics to support both sync/async idioms and clearer resource safety, and (3) automated changelog generation from PR metadata and semantic commit messages. Goal is to minimize friction for customers migrating to v2 while reducing operational support burden from inconsistent language SDK behaviors.

Background & motivation:
- v1 SDKs implemented retries in ad-hoc ways: Python used urllib3 Retry wrappers, TS used a homegrown retry util, Go used context-level retries in examples. These differences led to inconsistent observability (mismatched metrics), surprising behavior on idempotency, and customer confusion about how to configure retries for streaming vs. non-streaming calls.
- Streaming ergonomics: customers requested nicer async interfaces (async iterators in Python, async generators in TS) and clearer cancellation/close patterns for Go. v1 streaming APIs also conflated chunk-level errors with terminal errors which complicated retries.
- Changelog automation: large SDK surface produces noisy manual changelogs. We want consistent machine-readable changelogs that surface deprecations and migration notes.

Design decisions (high level):
- Unify retry model across SDKs: implement a common RetrySpec with: max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, multiplier, retryable_statuses, idempotent_only flag. Languages expose idiomatic constructors but must produce equivalent runtime behavior.
- Default policy: set conservative defaults: max_attempts=3, exponential backoff starting at 200ms, multiplier=2.0, cap at 5s. Document that customers should set idempotent_only=true for non-idempotent endpoints.
- Streaming behavior: split streaming APIs into two clear surfaces: streaming_iter (pull-based; safe to retry between chunks only when server supports chunk-level idempotency) and streaming_non_retriable (push/continuous streams where retries are disabled). Provide convenience wrappers: Python async iterator + synchronous iterator with context manager; TS AsyncIterable + EventEmitter bridge; Go channel + CloseWithError pattern.
- Deprecations: mark v1 streaming method stream() and the top-level globalRetries config as deprecated. Provide automated linter rule to detect use of deprecated patterns in internal examples and CI.
- Changelog automation: CI job sdk/changelog-bot reads merged PR labels (type:fix, type:feat, type:breaking, scope:python|typescript|go) and conventional commit messages to assemble a draft changelog categorized by language and by deprecations/migrations. The job emits a PR comment with generated markdown and creates a draft release note.

Migration guide (concise examples):
- Python (v1 -> v2):
  Old (v1):
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(api_key=KEY, global_retries=True)
  for chunk in c.stream("/generate"):
      process(chunk)

  New (v2):
  from redwood import Client, RetrySpec
  retry = RetrySpec(max_attempts=3, initial_backoff_ms=200, multiplier=2.0, retryable_statuses=[500,502,503])
  c = Client(api_key=KEY, retries=retry)
  # pull-based, safe to iterate in async contexts
  async for chunk in c.streaming_iter("/generate", idempotent=False):
      process(chunk)

  Notes: the new streaming_iter auto-closes the underlying HTTP connection when iteration ends or an exception is raised. To explicitly cancel, call await stream.aclose().

- TypeScript (v1 -> v2):
  Old (v1):
  const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: KEY, retry: { enabled: true } })
  c.stream('/generate').on('data', (chunk) => handle(chunk))

  New (v2):
  import { RedwoodClient, RetrySpec } from '@redwood/sdk'
  const retry = new RetrySpec({ maxAttempts: 3, initialBackoffMs: 200 })
  const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: KEY, retries: retry })
  for await (const chunk of c.streamingIter('/generate', { idempotent: false })) {
    handle(chunk)
  }

  Notes: If you need an EventEmitter API for integration with existing code, use c.streamingEmitter('/generate') which wraps the AsyncIterable with safe backpressure handling and an explicit .close() method.

- Go (v1 -> v2):
  Old (v1):
  client := redwood.NewClient(KEY)
  stream, _ := client.Stream("/generate")
  for { chunk, err := stream.Recv(); ... }

  New (v2):
  retry := redwood.RetrySpec{MaxAttempts:3, InitialBackoffMs:200, Multiplier:2.0}
  client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithAPIKey(KEY), redwood.WithRetries(retry))
  ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
  defer cancel()
  ch, err := client.StreamingIter(ctx, "/generate", redwood.StreamOptions{Idempotent:false})
  for chunk := range ch {
    handle(chunk)
  }

  Notes: Go StreamingIter returns a channel plus an error-returning goroutine. To explicitly cancel, call cancel(); underlying connection will shut down gracefully.

Compatibility & breaking changes:
- Default retry behavior tightened compared to some v1 usages; customers relying on unlimited retries must set explicit RetrySpec.
- v1 globalRetries boolean removed; map to RetrySpec in migration.
- stream() naming changed and behavior clarified. Deprecation window: two minor releases (2.0.0 -> 2.2.0) with runtime warnings in v2.0 and compilation-time linter hints.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Language SDK unit & integration tests updated to use a shared test matrix (see github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tests/matrix). Add golden test for streaming cancellation semantics.
- Canary release: publish v2.0.0-beta packages for Python/TS/Go; invite 5 early adopter customers to test migration guide.
- Observability: emit metrics: sdk.retry.attempts, sdk.retry.success_rate, sdk.stream.cancelled, sdk.stream.errors with language tag.

Changelog automation details:
- CI step: .github/workflows/changelog.yml triggered on release branch. Steps: (1) fetch merged PRs since last tag; (2) map PR labels to categories; (3) extract conventional commit summary from merged commits when present; (4) generate per-language sections and a MigrationNotes section (automatically detect any PR containing "migration"/"deprecate"); (5) post as draft release notes and create CHANGELOG-draft.md in the release PR.
- PR-level metadata: require PRs touching SDK surface to include one of the allowed labels (type:fix|feat|breaking) and a migration-mdx entry when breaking. Lint checks enforce labels.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Do we allow streaming retries for partial-idempotent endpoints with server-side resume tokens? Proposed: provide opt-in ResumeToken support in an extension namespace, not in core RetrySpec. This allows us to avoid widening defaults while enabling advanced customers.
- How to track cross-language parity for newly added flags? We'll schedule biweekly parity reviews with library owners.

Links & artifacts:
- Migration doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.company/sdk/v2-migration (internal)
- Implementation PR (TS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1245
- Retry spec design notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RetrySpecDraft
- Changelog automation job: .github/workflows/changelog.yml
- Test matrix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/main/tests/matrix

Acceptance criteria:
- All three SDKs expose a RetrySpec API and implement default behavior documented in the design doc.
- Streaming APIs present the new recommended surfaces and include cancellation examples in README for each language.
- Deprecation warnings emitted at runtime for v1 patterns; linter catches deprecated usages in our internal examples.
- Changelog CI step creates a human-readable draft and a machine-readable JSON summary attached to the release artifact.

Rollout notes for on-call and support:
- Create a dedicated support playbook for common migration errors: mismatch in retryable status codes, double-wrapping retries (SDK+customer proxy), cancellation leaks.
- Add a dashboard tile surfacing "migration beta traffic" by SDK version and errors by endpoint.
